title: Paired systolic–diastolic covariance fails to improve cross-sample classification of reported diabetes beyond mean pressures and marginal variability
abstract: We tested whether pairing, usually discarded when summarizing repeated clinic blood pressures, improves classification of self-reported diagnosed diabetes. A prespecified ridge-logistic model fitted in NHANES2005–2006 (n=3026,308 cases) was frozen and tested in independently recruited NHANES2009–2010 (n=5156,615 cases). Adding within-visit systolic–diastolic sample covariance to demographics, BMI, blood-pressure means and standard deviations, and medication indicators changed AUC from0.834132 to0.831909 (difference−0.002223;paired target bootstrap95% interval[−0.003739,−0.000868]). Log loss increased0.001243. Source-and-target refit uncertainty was broader:deltaAUC95% interval[−0.007502,0.000792]. This is a negative result for one candidate, not proof that covariance contains no physiological information or a diagnostic evaluation against glucose/HbA1c.
